description: We are a team of four students participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project, Earth Symphony, transforms Earth science data into sound through an interactive web experience. We are passionate about technology, space, data analysis, and creativity. We welcome motivated members skilled in web development, software, Earth science, data visualization, music, sound design, AI. Teamwork, curiosity, and creativity are what matter most. Let's turn Earth data into a symphony! 🌍🎵
summary:
The Earth Information Jukebox is an accessibility-focused project that transforms NASA Earth science data into sound, making climate information more accessible to everyone, especially people who are blind or visually impaired.

Our project uses NASA's Global Surface Temperature Anomaly dataset (GISTEMP v4) to explore how Earth's temperature has changed over time. We collect, clean, and analyze the scientific data, then transform numerical patterns into sound using data sonification techniques.

By exploring sound patterns such as pitch, rhythm, and intensity, users can experience climate trends through listening rather than relying only on visual charts and graphs.

Our goal is to make Earth science more inclusive, interactive, and engaging while raising awareness about climate change. Sonification complements traditional scientific visualization and provides an alternative way to explore complex environmental information.
details:
The Earth Information Jukebox is an inclusive data sonification project designed to make NASA Earth science information accessible through sound.

The project focuses on global surface temperature anomalies using NASA's GISTEMP v4 dataset. Our workflow includes collecting scientific data, inspecting and cleaning it, analyzing historical temperature trends, and preparing structured datasets for the sonification experience.

The project explores transforming numerical climate information into sound through different musical parameters, including pitch, rhythm, and intensity. These sound patterns aim to help users recognize changes and trends in Earth's temperature through listening.

Our main benefit is improving accessibility for people who are blind or visually impaired while offering an engaging alternative for anyone interested in climate science.

We used Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, CSV, and JSON for data processing and analysis, alongside software development tools and GitHub for collaboration and version control.

The creative aspect is connecting scientific data with musical expression. Our team considered scientific accuracy, data quality, accessibility, clarity of sound mappings, and the importance of complementing rather than replacing traditional visual scientific analysis.
